framework.what_review_means: Each authored argument, objection, Catholic reply and conclusion inspected, doctrinal source anchor identified, direct source identifiers checked against live stage map; distinct forms of evidence recorded.
framework.what_certification_requires: Every substantive English and French stage proposition compared with full original passage, opponent attributed only to proven actual proponent, precise magisterial level and Catholic moral object verified; competing original objections represented; human theological editorial signoff for disputed applications.
not_equal_to_certification: a legal or clinical publication describing a phenomenon
a book title or library catalogue page
a synthetic objection labelled only as an example
framework.claim_independent_review: An assistant's source checks do not constitute ecclesiastical approbation or imprimatur.

cases.doctrinal_evidence_note: Mill IV limits social coercion; does not reduce all private morality to a harm test.
The institution teaches necessary consent, not its sufficiency for every moral question.
VS 78-81 directly addresses moral object and intention; Fletcher primary wording remains unchecked.
Intrinsic evil means object incompatible with the good; personal culpability is not uniform.
Jesus and Paul give principles; new technologies are not enumerated in the Gospels.
St Paul's created-order and bodily arguments require interpretation, not dismissal as ancient.
Claimed doctrinal changes require proposition-by-proposition comparison and magisterial level.
DV 28-30 and 38 distinguish sincere conscience and doctrinal dissent.
Expert disagreement alone does not imply an authoritatively taught norm is optional.
Habits affect voluntary acts differently; addiction science does not quantify personal guilt.
Freud's historical repression critique cannot be equated to the Catholic virtue of chastity.
Small qualitative priest sample cannot show celibacy universally causes dysfunction.
Intention to marry is not the presently established marriage bond.
Pew records cohabiters' stated motivations, not a causal benefit of cohabitation.
Deliberate lust differs from the involuntary first glance; objection is illustrative.
Flirtation requires intention and concrete relationship commitments, not a universal gesture rule.
Premarital deliberate sexual acts distinct from ordinary affection; §§7 and 9.
Genuine loyalty and affection do not by themselves define the Catholic understanding of marriage.
Canon 1084 §3: sterility does not prohibit or nullify marriage; impotence differs.
Procreation and education are classical ends alongside mutual love; childless marriage remains valid.
Separation for safety must be distinguished from dissolution of a valid bond.
Canon 1085: civil divorce does not itself establish freedom to remarry.
The marital state does not turn every jointly agreed act into a licit act.
Humanae Vitae 13 disallows a conjugal act imposed against a spouse's reasonable wishes.
Manual §1624 includes gestures sustaining affection beyond immediate preparatory foreplay.
Conjugal exclusivity is not waived by mutual consent to third-party sexual partners.
Completed rectal intercourse distinguished from uncertain incidental/preparatory subcases.
Direct contraception and proportionate reasons to postpone conception are separate moral issues.
Pius XII distinguishes periodic abstinence and direct contraception; motives remain relevant.
Continence and deliberately contracepted intercourse are not the same chosen act.
§59 limits willing participation of a reluctant spouse; never validates contraception.
§9 distinguishes objective gravity from factors that diminish subjective culpability.
Consent does not settle the moral analysis of pornography; PP source admits potential harms.
Private spousal digital images lack a universal device-specific magisterial decree; prudent risk remains.
§8 addresses sexual acts while distinguishing mere inclination from personal fault.
Infertility does not prevent marriage; procreative bodily-act ontology needs separate reasoning.
1986 CDF §10 condemns violent malice alongside its sexual-ethics judgment.
Psychiatric diagnostic status cannot alone establish a moral conclusion about acts.
CDF institutional argument is distinct from unsupported empirical predictions about social harm.
Cultural roles vary while embodiment has moral relevance; individual sex-development variations need precision.
Actual gender-dysphoria distress and clinical effects are empirical matters distinct from moral anthropology.
Charitable respect does not logically mandate assent; specific language choices require prudence.
§60 has a medical exception for genital abnormalities; SOC8 is clinical, not Church teaching.
§§12-16 distinguish legitimate fertility assistance from replacing the marital act.
II.A.3 rejects surrogate motherhood independently of commercial exploitation.
Physiological arousal is not consent; RAINN is contrary evidence, not a defender of the misconception.
Impairment and capacity are contextual; moral principle does not decide each legal case.
1974 doctrinal argument acknowledges different historical positions on fetal ensoulment. Original Kuhse-Singer chapter summary now replaces a book catalogue as opposing provenance.
2009 CDF defends life while explicitly recognizing the rape survivor's serious pastoral needs.
Urgent ectopic medical care and CDF principle are distinct from debated method-specific moral objects.
Francis 2013 criticizes disproportionate emphasis, not the substance of sexual doctrine.
Contemporary sexual pressures do not prove universal moral impossibility.
Purity/shame research is correlational and not causal evidence against all Catholic teaching.
Fletcher's agape differs from slogan love-is-love; direct first-hand attribution unresolved.
Scientific observations and theological moral propositions answer distinct kinds of questions.
